analysis: spatially blocked development comparison followed by a single untouched external-cohort evaluation

target.estimand: measured dry forage yield in kg DM/ha from clipped quadrat samples; Mendeley measurement timing relative to clipping is not documented
target.feature: grass height in cm measured at the sampling points in the same Mendeley campaigns; measurement timing relative to clipping is not documented

developmentCohort.population: forage samples from two managed-pasture farms in western São Paulo, Brazil

developmentValidation.foldConstruction: Leave one connected farm/field component out; connect field components that contain exact-coordinate aliases; preserve all campaigns and same-coordinate observations in one held-out block.
developmentValidation.coverageGate: Before fitting, fail the model comparison if realized coverage or nonempty held-out blocks falls below the fixed threshold; do not reduce the buffer after inspecting target errors.
developmentValidation.primaryMetric: equal-weight mean of within-block MAE (kg DM/ha)

fixedCandidates.name: Ridge height-only
fixedCandidates.fit: standardize on training fold only, Ridge alpha=1.0

fixedCandidates.name: quadratic height-only
fixedCandidates.fit: degree-2 polynomial after training-fold centering/scaling; no degree or knot search

developmentValidation.selectionAndRetention: Select no challenger using the external cohort. Retain a challenger to OLS only if primary block-macro MAE is at least 10% lower on identical rows, row-weighted RMSE worsens by no more than 5%, and no farm/campaign subgroup with at least 20 scored spatial groups worsens by more than 10%; otherwise use OLS as the fixed reference or report no improvement. The quadratic model is development-only for the aggregated external outcome because applying a nonlinear model to paddock mean height is not algebraically equivalent to averaging point-level predictions.
developmentValidation.uncertainty: Do not interpret 13 spatial blocks nested in two farms as a population-level confidence interval. Report block-level results and coverage; no nominal prediction-interval or calibration claim.

externalEvaluation.population: cool-season grass-legume pasture under mob and rotational grazing, northeastern United States, 2015-2018
externalEvaluation.target: mean PGFM in kg/ha, aggregating available plot-level quadrat yields within treatment x replicate x study year x Julian day; do not impute missing quadrats
externalEvaluation.feature: published pre-grazing mean sward height in cm at the same treatment x replicate x study year x Julian day level
externalEvaluation.modelFreeze: Select the final candidate and all hyperparameters from Mendeley spatial-block CV only; refit that fixed candidate once on all 234 Mendeley rows, then evaluate once on the 64 Dryad rows. Dryad outcomes must not alter candidate, transform, or threshold choices.
externalEvaluation.supportAnalysis: Mendeley height support is 2-56 cm. Report all Dryad rows as the primary external test and separate metrics for the predeclared in-support and above-support rows; mark out-of-support predictions explicitly as extrapolation. Do not clip features or filter out-of-support cases after seeing residuals.
metrics: metrics by treatment, calendar year, Julian day, and support status
externalEvaluation.uncertainty: Report each of the eight paddock-group errors and the distribution across groups. Do not present a narrow confidence interval or claim a calibrated prediction interval from eight paddocks.
externalEvaluation.scopeLimit: This is a distinct temperate pasture biomass evaluation against a related but not strictly identical sampling estimand. It cannot validate tropical Brazilian performance, animal DMI, ADG, or the complete engine.
externalEvaluation.supportComposition: 40 of 64 Dryad rows are within Mendeley numeric height support, but Mendeley has only 51 of 234 rows in this range; all 24 above-support Dryad rows are MOB treatment, so support status is confounded with grazing treatment and calendar year. This stratum is not a balanced transport comparison.

preserveGroups: paddock across all years and harvest dates

amendments.reason: Primary Mendeley repository description confirms that height and biomass were collected at the same points in the second and third campaigns but does not state measurement sequence relative to clipping.
amendments.change: Clarified the Mendeley estimand and feature timing as undocumented relative to clipping. No model, threshold, candidate, fold, or external outcome was changed based on Dryad results. The selected final model was affine OLS, for which applying it to the matched mean height is aggregation-compatible.
